formats.key: Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)
effects: Once anyone submits the signature to permit() before the deadline, the WBTC allowance that the owner (the signer) gives the spender is set to exactly `value`. Any earlier allowance for that spender is replaced (ERC20PermitUpgradeable.permit -> _approve(owner, spender, value)).
The signer's permit nonce goes up by one (_useNonce). This is bookkeeping only.

The signature is only valid under the domain name 'Wrapped BTC', version '1', chainId 59144 and verifyingContract = the proxy 0x3aab…a9b4. The proxy constructor's _data calls initialize('Wrapped BTC','WBTC',8), and __ERC20Permit_init(name) sets version '1'.
formats.shown: The intent 'Authorize spending of tokens', with the spender (raw address), the max spending amount in WBTC (shown as 'Unlimited' at or above 2^255), the valid-until date and the owner. The nonce is hidden.

findings.title: The Permit primary type has no test case, so no rendering of the WBTC amount, the Unlimited message or the date is checked.
findings.evidence: FORMATS.md: 'cases: 0 (no tx)' for Permit(address owner,address spender,uint256 value,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline).
findings.fix: Add an EIP-712 test case with a finite value (8 decimals, WBTC) and one with value >= 2^255 to check the 'Unlimited' message.
